name: MAX3078EESA+
title: MAX3070E–MAX3079E: 3.3 V, ±15 kV ESD, fail-safe, hot-swap RS-485/RS-422 transceivers
summary: A family of ten RS-485/RS-422 transceivers running from 3.3 V, each holding a single driver and a single receiver. The bus pins survive ±15 kV Human Body Model ESD, the receiver reads high with open, shorted or idle terminated inputs, and a 1/8 unit-load input lets 256 nodes share a bus. Parts differ by duplex, driver edge rate (250 kbps, 500 kbps or 16 Mbps) and enable pins; the MAX3079E selects all of these by pin and adds polarity inversion. MAX3078EESA+ is the 16 Mbps half-duplex part in an 8-pin SO, lead-free, -40 °C to +85 °C.

circuits.title: Typical full-duplex operating circuit, 14-pin (MAX3070E, MAX3073E, MAX3076E)
circuits.description: A point-to-point link on two twisted pairs. U1's driver outputs Y and Z feed the far transceiver's receiver, and the far driver feeds U1's A and B. Each pair carries a terminating resistor Rt across its two wires at the receiving end. U1's supply pin has a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground; DE, RE, DI and RO are the logic connections, and the three N.C. pins are left unconnected.

circuits.description: Two half-duplex transceivers share one twisted pair, A to A and B to B, with a resistor Rt across the pair at each end. Each node's DE and RE choose whether it talks or listens. circuits.title: Line repeater, full duplex (Figure 11)
circuits.description: One full-duplex transceiver regenerates a long line: the incoming pair lands on A and B with 120 Ω across it, RO is wired straight back to DI, and Y and Z drive the outgoing pair, also with 120 Ω across it. It extends a link past the 4000 ft that RS-485/RS-422 allows for one run. Applies to the MAX3070E, MAX3071E, MAX3073E, MAX3074E, MAX3076E, MAX3077E and the MAX3079E in full-duplex mode.
notes: Supply and ground are not drawn; RE and DE are drawn as open control lines.

circuits.title: Typical half-duplex RS-485 network (Figure 12)
circuits.description: Four half-duplex transceivers hang on one twisted pair, every A on one wire and every B on the other. The pair is terminated with 120 Ω across it at both ends, and the nodes between the ends tap on with short stubs. Each node has its own DI, DE, RO and RE. Applies to the MAX3072E, MAX3075E, MAX3078E and the MAX3079E in half-duplex mode.
notes: When a MAX3079E is set for half duplex its bus pins are Y and Z; supply and ground are not drawn.

circuits.title: Typical full-duplex RS-485 network (Figure 13)
circuits.description: Four full-duplex transceivers on two twisted pairs. U1's driver (Y, Z) talks on one pair to the receivers (A, B) of every other node; the drivers of U2, U3 and U4 all share the second pair back to U1's receiver. Both pairs carry 120 Ω across them at each end. Applies to the MAX3070E, MAX3073E, MAX3076E and the MAX3079E in full-duplex mode.

operation.text: Ten 3.3 V RS-485/RS-422 transceivers, each a single driver plus a single receiver. They differ in duplex (half, full, or pin-selected on the MAX3079E), driver slew rate (250 kbps, 500 kbps or 16 Mbps; selectable on the MAX3079E) and whether DE and RE pins with shutdown exist (absent on the 8-pin full-duplex MAX3071E, MAX3074E, MAX3077E). MAX3078E is the 16 Mbps half-duplex 8-pin part, with enables and shutdown.

MAX3070E/71E/72E have slew-limited drivers for up to 250 kbps, lowering EMI and reflections from poorly terminated cables. MAX3073E/74E/75E are slew-limited for up to 500 kbps. MAX3076E/77E/78E have no slew limiting and reach 16 Mbps. The slew-limited MAX3072E and MAX3075E, and the MAX3079E in its two slew-limited modes, tolerate imperfect termination better.

The receiver threshold lies between −50 mV and −200 mV, so RO is high when A − B ≥ −50 mV, low when A − B ≤ −200 mV, and high with the inputs open, shorted, or on a terminated bus with every driver off (the termination pulls the difference to 0 V, a 50 mV minimum margin). The threshold stays within the ±200 mV of EIA/TIA-485.

The receivers of MAX3070E to MAX3075E, and of the MAX3079E in its 250 kbps and 500 kbps modes, filter the input as well as having hysteresis, for noise immunity on slow differential edges. The filter adds 25 % to receiver propagation delay.

DE and RE are hot-swap inputs (all parts except MAX3071E/74E/77E, which have no enables). While VCC rises, an internal pull keeps DE at logic 0 and RE at logic 1 so a board plugged into a live bus does not upset it while its controller's outputs are still high impedance (leakage up to ±10 µA) or parasitic capacitance couples VCC or GND in. On DE, a 10 µs timer turns on M2, a 500 µA sink, and sets a latch that turns on M1, a 100 µA sink, both pulling DE to GND through 5 kΩ; M2 can hold DE low against up to 100 pF of parasitic capacitance. After 10 µs M2 turns off and M1 stays on against three-state leakage until an external driver overcomes it; the latch then resets, M1 turns off and DE becomes an ordinary high-impedance CMOS input. The circuit re-arms whenever VCC falls below 1 V. RE has a matching circuit of two PMOS devices pulling it to VCC.

SRL picks the driver edge rate with three levels from a three-state driver: open (or high impedance) for 250 kbps, VCC for 500 kbps, GND for 16 Mbps; it may change during operation without interrupting data. TXP and RXP invert the driver and receiver polarity to fix a pair wired backwards; low, grounded or open is normal (internal pulldowns), high inverts. With RXP high the receiver threshold is positive. H/F low, open or grounded gives full duplex, laid out like the MAX3070E; H/F high gives half duplex, switching the receiver inputs onto Y and Z while the A and B input resistors stay connected to pins 12 and 11.

RE high together with DE low enters shutdown (not on MAX3071E/74E/77E); supply current is typically 50 nA. The part does not enter shutdown if that state lasts under 50 ns and is sure to enter it after 600 ns, so RE and DE may be driven at the same time. Coming out of shutdown is slower (the tZH(SHDN) and tZL(SHDN) figures) than coming out of the plain disabled state (tZH and tZL).

The output stage folds its current limit back, which protects against shorts over the whole common-mode range, and thermal shutdown puts the driver outputs in high impedance when the die gets too hot (175 °C typ, 15 °C hysteresis).

All pins have ESD structures; the bus pins (Y, Z, A, B) withstand ±15 kV Human Body Model and ±6 kV IEC 1000-4-2 contact discharge, in normal operation, shutdown and powered down, without latchup. IEC 1000-4-2 has higher peak current than the Human Body Model because of its lower series resistance, so its withstand voltage is generally lower.
Each receiver input is 1/8 unit load (96 kΩ) against the standard 12 kΩ, so up to 256 transceivers fit on one line.

RS-485/RS-422 allows runs up to 4000 ft; longer lines use the repeater of Figure 11. To keep reflections down, each end of the line gets a resistor equal to the cable's characteristic impedance, and stubs branching from the main run are kept as short as possible.
The MAX3077EMSA/PR is the -55 °C to +125 °C version of the MAX3077E in 8-pin SO and meets its specification over temperature.
